sequence_description: SAML OneTimeUse replay across distinct sessions: perform a successful SAML login with a fixed Assertion/@ID and OneTimeUse, then attempt to replay the exact same assertion ID in a second login attempt. Expected: second attempt rejected (anti-replay).
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_replay_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_replay_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted replayed SAML assertion with OneTimeUse (anti-replay failure).

sequence_description: Replay the exact same SAML Assertion/@ID without OneTimeUse across two login attempts; expected rejection on second use if Casdoor implements assertion ID replay cache even without OneTimeUse.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_i2_saml_replay_saml2_http_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_i2_saml_replay_saml2_http_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Casdoor accepted a replayed SAML assertion with the same Assertion/@ID (anti-replay failure).

sequence_description: Exchange a subject_token for a new token, revoke all sessions, then attempt token exchange again using the old subject_token; expected rejection if revocation invalidates the subject token for further exchanges.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_i2_exchange_revoke_ex2_http_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_i2_exchange_revoke_ex2_http_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Casdoor allowed token exchange using a revoked subject_token, minting fresh credentials after logout (freshness failure).

sequence_description: SAML flow coherence: attempt to authenticate using a forged SAMLResponse that claims an unexpected IdP entity_id (Issuer) while still targeting the same application/provider endpoint. Broker should reject if it binds assertions to the configured provider/issuer.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_saml_wrong_issuer_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_saml_wrong_issuer_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Broker accepted SAML assertion with unexpected Issuer (provider/session binding failure).

sequence_description: Unicode normalization collision test via SAML: login twice with visually identical but byte-distinct NameID/email (NFC vs NFD). Broker should not collapse distinct upstream principals into one downstream subject unless it intentionally normalizes and treats them as same principal.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_saml_nfc_entity_id != user_saml_nfd_entity_id
Evaluation: user_saml_nfc_entity_id='admin' != 'admin' → False
Implication: Unicode-normalization-variant upstream principals (NFC vs NFD) collapsed into the same downstream subject

sequence_description: I4: Attempt cross-IdP principal collision by spoofing SAML Issuer (idp_entity_id) while keeping NameID/email constant vs a different principal, checking whether Casdoor collapses identities across IdP boundaries.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_A_entity_id != user_C_entity_id
Evaluation: user_A_entity_id='shared-nameid' != 'shared-nameid' → False
Implication: Principal binding violated: same NameID/email from different (spoofed) SAML Issuer collapsed into the same downstream subject

sequence_description: Application tag restrictions should constrain who can sign in; attempt to bypass sign-in authorization gate by using brokered SAML login for a user lacking required tag.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_charlie_saml_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_charlie_saml_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SAML brokered login bypassed application tag restriction, granting a session to a user without required tags (I5).
